Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remembered it, but i think that must be a good sign?

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Don't remember.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was not scarifying, since I had very few options due to late enrolment in the general system at the university. But in the end i ended being very glad for the more or less random coursed in ended up being enrolled in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This thanks to the great professors at the university.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Appropriate but a bit varying from course to course. Some of them was clearly more easy than most courses on UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Overall the courses where more focused on theory and less on empirical practice than i am used to from UCPH. Moreover they where characterised by being much more individual than i am used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Contemporary China. Conflicts, Peace-Building and International Regulation. Europe as A Global Actor. Contemporary International Migration. Sociology of Modernity.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contemporary China. Conflicts, Peace-Building and International Regulation.
